correctness.rationale: For every finite field and n>=3, the bipartite ladder alternating weighted adjacency matrix is permutation-congruent to [0 T;-T^T 0], where T ranges bijectively over all unrestricted n-by-n tridiagonal matrices. The proof tracks the last-pair image of solutions to successive T rows; the five actual subspace types 0,H,V,O,F collapse into 0,H,X,F because V and oblique lines give equal aggregated transition weights. Explicit first/terminal row weights, including terminal dummy-variable normalization, produce u M^(n-2) v with nullity exponent n-rank(T). For odd q only, the twisted class-two group algebra of a central character with alternating rank 2r has q^(2n-2r) simple blocks of degree q^r, yielding the formula for all degrees. Independent brute-force ranks for q=2,n=3; q=3,n=3; q=2,n=4 exactly match, as do total edge-labeling counts. Finite checks are corroboration of, not proof for, arbitrary n or q; the n=2 known four-cycle boundary is excluded from claimed novelty.
